correctness.rationale: The positive evaluation \(P(\pi)+2P(\pi-\delta)\) cancels both free coefficients and gives the sharp upper bound. The stated coefficients make a quadratic \(R\) the Hermite interpolant of \(g(y)=A\cos((\arccos y)/m)\) at \(y=1\) and \(y=-1/2\), with the latter a double node. The hypergeometric series has negative nonconstant coefficients, so the third derivative of \(g\) is positive on \((-1,1)\); the Hermite remainder therefore gives \(R\ge g\). Folding \(\arccos(\cos(m\phi))/m\le\phi\) transfers this majorization to global nonnegativity. Equality in the upper certificate plus the derivative condition at the interior contact uniquely determines the two free coefficients. The boundary case \(m=2\) satisfies the same proof. The bundled checker corroborates contacts, interpolation, and sampled positivity without replacing the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The prescribed-support problem asks for exact constants for structured sparse frequency sets. The doubled family \(\{m,2m\}\) is natural rather than an arbitrary slice: one allowed higher harmonic is doubled to obtain the other. The theorem upgrades a known strict-improvement statement at the added frequency \(2m\) to an exact closed form with a unique extremizer for every \(m\), while correctly subsuming the previously solved \(m=2\) case. The Hermite-majorant mechanism also explains the parameter dependence structurally, so the result is more than isolated computation.
